# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll explore the codebase to find the transaction labeling logic and the edge-case faults described in the forum digest.

# Transaction labeling codebase report

## 1. Project structure overview

Flask microservice for Indian bank statement enrichment. Single commit (`import codebase`); **no test suite**.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # gunicorn on :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, sklearn, …
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app bootstrap
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP API + per-bank pipeline
        ├── BankScripts/                # ~35 bank-specific categorizer modules
        │   ├── HDFC.py, ICICI.py, Axis.py, SBI.py, Kotak.py, …
        │   └── …
        └── UtilityScripts/             # shared post-processing
            ├── AppUtil.py              # DF cleanup + sep_by_* / py_extract helpers
            ├── RegexConstants.py       # cross-bank purpose/merchant regexes
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py   # bank-specific narration patterns
            ├── Purpose.py              # transactionSubcategory + merchantType
            ├── CleanName.py            # merchant name normalization (~2k lines)
            ├── SalaryDetection.py      # ML/heuristic salary clustering
            ├── InternalPayment.py      # self-transfer detection
            ├── PFMCategorization.py    # PFM L1/L2 categories
            ├── SimpleDescription.py
            ├── CardCleanNames.py / CardPurpose.py
            ├── RecurrentTxns.py
            └── Transaction*Enums.py
```

### Pipeline (`/categorizeTransaction`)

For each bank, `Controller.py` runs roughly:

1. Bank script → `transactionCategory`, initial `partyName`, sometimes `transactionSubcategory` / `merchantType`
2. Credit-card path: `card_clean_names` + `card_purpose`
3. `purpose()` → subcategory + merchant type from narration/party
4. `clean_names()` → canonical `partyName` / merchant fixes
5. `internal_payment()` if account holder present
6. `salary_detection()` for `SAVING`
7. Optional PFM + simple description

Default category when nothing matches is almost always **`TRANSFER`**.

Core helpers in `AppUtil.py`:

- `sep_by_(desc, n1, n2)` → slash-split join of segments `[n1:n2]`
- `sep_by_dash` / `sep_by_wave` / `sep_by_star` / …
- `py_extract(desc, pat, index)` → regex capture group

---

## 2. Key file paths

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | Routes; wires bank → purpose → clean_names → salary |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` | Category + party extraction per bank |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` | Sub-tags (salary, bounce type, loan, bills, …) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` | Payee/merchant cleanup after bank extract |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | Shared SALARY/LOAN/BOUNCE/… regexes |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | HDFC/Kotak/SBI/… narration patterns |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` | Frequency/clustering salary promotion |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` | Fuzzy match party ↔ account holder |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | Split/extract primitives |

### How categories are assigned

Bank scripts build ordered `conditions_choices` lists and apply `np.select` (first match wins). Examples:

- Cheque: `CHQ`/`CLG`/`MICR` in description, or **numeric `remark`** as cheque number  
- Transfers: NEFT/RTGS/IMPS/UPI keywords  
- Bounce/return: `CHQ RTN`, `REJECT:`, ECS return, etc.  
- Offsetting pairs: `shift(1)` debit→credit same amount/description → bounce or reversal  

### How payees are extracted

Bank-specific slash/dash/regex rules → `partyName`, then `CleanName.clean_names` overwrites known merchants. Direction words stripped unevenly (SBI has `TRF_STOP_WORDS`; others partial).

### How sub-tags work

`Purpose.purpose()` maps description/party into `transactionSubcategory` (salary, loan repayment, utility bill, technical bounce, …) and `merchantType`. Bank scripts can set subcategory earlier (e.g. HDFC bare-numeric salary).

---

## 3. Tests

**None found.** No `tests/`, `test_*.py`, or specs. Only a one-line git history (`import codebase`). Regressions must be validated manually or with new tests.

---

## 4. Bug-focused suspicious code

### A) Long all-numeric credit → generic TRANSFER (was cheque deposit); bare-numeric salary lost sub-tag

**Cheque via remark (length-sensitive):**

Many banks treat short all-numeric `remark` as cheque number:

```58:59:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Axis.py
        [transactions.remark.str.contains("^[0-9]{5,6}$", na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("DEBIT"), "CHEQUE_PAID"],
        [transactions.remark.str.contains("^[0-9]{5,6}$", na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT"), "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT"],
```

Same idea elsewhere with different bounds:

- Axis/PNB/Indusind/BOM: `^[0-9]{5,6}$`
- Kotak/BOB: `^[0-9]{3,5}$`
- YES/UCO: `^[0-9]{3,6}$`
- RBL: `^[0-9]{1,3}$` only

If cheque/ref numbers are now **>6 digits** (or longer than bank max), they miss cheque rules and fall through to default **`TRANSFER`**.

**HDFC special case (very narrow):**

```100:100:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
        [(transactions.remark.str.len().eq(15)) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & transactions.remark.str.contains("^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}", na=False, case=False) , "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT"]
```

Only 15-char zero-padded `00000000000XXXXX`. Any other long numeric remark → **TRANSFER**.

**Bare-numeric salary — likely typo:**

```124:124:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
        [transactions.transactionCategory.eq("TRANSFER") & transactions.description.str.contains("^[0-9]{6}$", na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & (accountType=="SAVINGS") , "SALARY"],
```

Controller always uses **`SAVING`**, not `SAVINGS`:

```106:108:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py
       if accountType == "SAVING": 
          app.logger.info(f"Detecting Salary in {bank} Txns for accountUID {accountUID}")
          result = salary_detection(transactions)
```

So 6-digit description credits never get bank-level `SALARY` subcategory.

Downstream salary detection also **requires non-empty `partyName`**:

```50:50:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py
        transactions_sub = transactions_sub[transactions_sub['partyName'].str.len().gt(0) & transactions_sub['partyName'].notnull()]
```

Bare-numeric narrations usually extract empty party → salary_detection cannot promote them either.

`Purpose.py` salary rules need salary keywords (`SALARY`, `SAL_IMPS`, …) and exclude UPI/IMPS — bare codes won’t match.

---

### B) Narration opens with direction word → empty/wrong counterparty

**ICICI — capture-group index bug:**

```159:159:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("TRFR TO:|TRFR FROM:", na=False, case=False) , py_extract(transactions.description, pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)],
```

`index=0` is **TO/FROM**, not the name (`index=1`). Party becomes `"To"` / `"From"`.

Later cleanup blanks some junk (`^NA$`, etc.) but not bare direction words for this path.

**Axis — TRANSFER slash takes first segment:**

```146:147:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Axis.py
        [transactions.transactionCategory.eq("TRANSFER") & transactions.description.str.count("/").eq(2) , sep_by_(transactions.description,0,1)],
        [transactions.transactionCategory.eq("TRANSFER") & transactions.description.str.count("/").eq(1) , sep_by_(transactions.description,0,1)],
```

For `TO/John` or `FROM/Acme`, party = **`TO`/`FROM`**. Cleanup only drops exact `^FROM$` / `^TRANSFER$`:

```167:169:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Axis.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^TRANSFER TO ", na=False, case=False), transactions.partyName.replace(to_replace="^TRANSFER TO ", value="", regex=True)],
        [transactions.partyName.str.contains("^NA$|[Xx]xx|Remitter|Unregist|^[0-9]{4,}$|Discount On|^By Clg", na=False, case=False) , ""],
        [transactions.partyName.str.contains("^Razorpay$|^TRANSFER$|^EDC$|^[A-Z]$|^APY$|^ACH$|^ARD$|^FROM$|^TRANSFER$", na=False, case=False) , ""],
```

`To` after `.title()` may not match `^FROM$`; single letter `T` would blank, multi-char direction words may stick or become empty inconsistently.

**UnionBank — strips `Transfer|^To` after extract:**

```118:121:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/UnionBank.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^TRF? TO ", na=False, case=False)       , py_extract(transactions.description, pat="^TRF? TO (.*)", index=0)],
        ...
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^TO [A-Z]", na=False, case=False)       , py_extract(transactions.description, pat="^TO (.*)", index=0)],
```

Then:

```144:144:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/UnionBank.py
        [transactions.partyName.str.contains("Transfer|^To", na=False, case=False), transactions.partyName.replace(to_replace="Transfer|^To", value="", regex=True)]
```

`^To` only at start of party after title-case — edge cases remain.

**SBI is stronger** via `TRF_STOP_WORDS` in `BankRegexConstants.py` (strips `To Transfer`, `Transfer From`, `By Transfer`, etc.). Other banks lack equivalent breadth.

**Kotak FT patterns** generally capture *after* TO/FROM (`FT_PATTERN1 = "^FUNDS? TRF? TO (.*)"`) — better, but only when those patterns fire before weaker rules.

---

### C) Bill transfers `type/sub-type/numeric-ref/payee` → numeric ref as name

**ICICI `BIL/` extraction order (first match wins):**

```147:151:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^BIL/INFT/", na=False, case=False) & transactions.description.str.count("/").eq(3)  , sep_by_(transactions.description,2,3)],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^BIL/BPAY.*BBPS|^BIL/BBPS.*BBPS|^BIL/INFT|^BIL/NEFT", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_(transactions.description,4,5)],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^BIL/BPAY|^BIL/RCHG|^BIL/ONL", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_(transactions.description,3,4)],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^BIL/00[12].*/.*/NSP0.*/", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_(transactions.description,4,5)],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^BIL/00[12].*/.*/(?!(NSP))", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_(transactions.description,2,3).replace(to_replace='\d+', value='', regex=True)...],
```

Example: `BIL/BPAY/<type>/<numeric-ref>/<payee-name>`

- Segments: `[0]=BIL, [1]=BPAY, [2]=type, [3]=numeric-ref, [4]=payee`
- Line 149: `sep_by_(..., 3, 4)` → **numeric-ref**, not payee  
- BBPS path uses index 4 (payee) — plain BPAY does not  

Also `^BIL/001/.../(?!NSP)` uses index 2 (subtype), then strips digits — can wipe payee-like numeric pieces and leave wrong field.

**Axis bill-like paths:**

```121:121:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Axis.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^TRF/[0-9]+/[A-Z]", na=False, case=False)  , sep_by_(transactions.description,2,3)],
```

`TRF/<num>/<name>` → index 2 = name (OK).  
`TRF/<type>/<sub>/<num>/<name>` may hit generic UPI/IMPS `sep_by_(...,3,4)` and pick the wrong slot.

**HDFC payment-gateway extract:**

```176:179:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
        [transactions.transactionCategory.isin(["PAYMENT_VIA_PAYU",...]) , py_extract(..., ".*/[A-Z]{4}(.*)|.*/TECH{4}(.*)", index=0)],
```

Fragile against slash layouts where a numeric block sits where the letter-prefix group expects a name.

**Root issue:** fixed slash indices assume a single layout; when banks insert type/sub-type/ref before the name, the name index shifts right and the numeric ref is selected.

---

### D) Offsetting credit after matching debit → bounce instead of reversal

**ICICI (clear bounce-over-reversal):**

```49:50:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py
        [transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & transactions.type.shift(periods=1).eq("DEBIT") & transactions.amount.eq(transactions.amount.shift(periods=1)) & transactions.description.eq(transactions.description.shift(periods=1)) & transactions.description.str.contains("IMPS|NEFT|\\bUPI|RTGS", na=False, case=False), "REVERSAL"],
        [transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & transactions.type.shift(periods=1).eq("DEBIT") & transactions.amount.eq(transactions.amount.shift(periods=1)) & transactions.description.eq(transactions.description.shift(periods=1)) , "AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE"],
```

- Same-description debit→credit of equal amount is **REVERSAL** only if narration has IMPS/NEFT/UPI/RTGS.
- Everything else (ACH, SI, FT, internal transfer, bill pay, plain TRANSFER) becomes **`AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`**.

**HDFC — REVERSAL condition likely broken:**

```98:99:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
        [transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & transactions.type.shift(periods=1).eq("DEBIT") & transactions.amount.eq(transactions.amount.shift(periods=1)) & transactions.description.eq(transactions.description.shift(periods=2)) & transactions.description.str.contains("IMPS|NEFT|\\bUPI|RTGS", na=False, case=False), "REVERSAL"],
        [transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & transactions.type.shift(periods=1).eq("DEBIT") & transactions.amount.eq(transactions.amount.shift(periods=1)) & transactions.description.eq(transactions.description.shift(periods=1)), "AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE"],
```

REVERSAL compares description to **`shift(periods=2)`** (two rows back), not the immediately preceding debit. Adjacent equal IMPS/NEFT pairs often **fail REVERSAL** and hit **AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE** instead.

Also HDFC classifies many credit SI/ACH/EMI patterns as bounce by keyword alone (line 27), before pair logic.

**Saraswat** only has the IMPS/NEFT/UPI/RTGS REVERSAL pair rule (no broad bounce fallback). **StandardCharted** only bounce-pairs NACH DR IW.

**Purpose side-effect:** categories containing `BOUNCE` get subcategory cleared:

```172:174:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py
        [transactions.transactionCategory.str.contains("REFUND|WITHDRAWAL|CHARGES|BOUNCE|PENALTY|FEES|VERIFICATION|IMPS_REVERSAL", na=False, case=False) & ... , ""],
```

So mis-tagged bounces also lose useful sub-tags / merchant types.

---

## 5. Patterns / “recent changes”

Git has a single import commit — no incremental history. Likely regression sources in the imported logic itself:

| Area | Fragile pattern |
|------|-----------------|
| Cheque | Hard-coded remark digit lengths (`{5,6}`, `{3,5}`, HDFC 15-char zero-pad) |
| Salary | `SAVINGS` vs `SAVING`; salary_detection requires partyName |
| Party | Fixed `sep_by_` indices; direction word as capture group 0 |
| Bounce/reversal | Broad equal-amount pair → bounce; HDFC `shift(2)` on REVERSAL |
| np.select | First-true wins; ordering bugs when general rules precede specific ones |

---

## 6. Highest-priority fix targets (by bug)

| Bug | Primary files | Likely fix direction |
|-----|---------------|----------------------|
| **A** cheque | `Axis.py`, `PNB.py`, `HDFC.py`, `Kotak.py`, `YES.py`, … | Widen/normalize numeric remark cheque detection; don’t require exact pad length |
| **A** salary | `HDFC.py:124` (`SAVINGS`→`SAVING`); `SalaryDetection.py` partyName filter; `Purpose.py` | Fix enum string; allow bare-numeric salary path without party |
| **B** | `ICICI.py:159` (`index=0`→`1`); `Axis.py` TRANSFER `sep_by_(0,1)`; add direction strip like SBI `TRF_STOP_WORDS` | Capture name after TO/FROM; strip leading direction tokens |
| **C** | `ICICI.py` BIL/BPAY indices (~147–151); similar slash bill rules in Axis/HDFC | Prefer last non-numeric slash field as payee; don’t use fixed mid index for ref |
| **D** | `ICICI.py:49–50`, `HDFC.py:98–99` | Fix HDFC `shift(2)`→`shift(1)`; treat same-narration offsetting credit as REVERSAL unless bounce/return keywords; narrow AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE |

---

## 7. Mental model summary

```
narration + remark + type
        │
        ▼
BankScripts.categorize_*  ──► transactionCategory
                          ──► partyName (raw extract)
                          ──► optional subcategory
        │
        ▼
Purpose.purpose           ──► transactionSubcategory, merchantType
        │
        ▼
CleanName.clean_names     ──► normalized partyName / merchant overrides
        │
        ▼
InternalPayment / SalaryDetection / PFM (optional)
```

Labeling is almost entirely **ordered regex + `np.select`**, not ML (except salary clustering). Edge cases in remark length, slash field position, direction prefixes, and debit/credit pair heuristics explain all four bugs without needing missing external config.

Let me look at py_extract more carefully. The regex is `TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)` with index=0. In pandas str.extract, groups are 0-indexed for capture groups... Actually looking at the code:
The regex bug you spotted in `py_extract` is definitely the root cause for the salary-credit case. When the narration is a bare numeric code, the pattern `TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)` is matching the whole string as group 0, so `index=0` pulls the entire description instead of 1 (the actual name). That’s why the sub-tag disappears.

For the direction-word transfers, the current `sep_by_` logic is inverted. When the narration starts with `TO/` or `FROM/`, `count("/") == 1` and `sep_by_(0,1)` returns the direction word itself (“TO” or “FROM”), which then gets blanked by the cleanup rule that targets `^FROM$`. Switching to `sep_by_(1,2)` would give the name correctly.

The HDFC cheque pattern is too narrow. The 15-character zero-padded pattern only catches the exact `000000000 00XXXXX` form; anything longer (16-char cheque numbers or non-padded references) is missed.
